Pathophysiology
Evolving pathophysiologic mechanisms in diverticulosis and 
diverticulitis suggest chronic inflammation, alterations in co-
lonic microbiota, disturbed colonic sensorimotor function, and 
abnormal colon motility have likely interrelated roles in the 
development of diverticular disease (Strate et al, 2012). 
Complications of diverticular disease range from painless, mild 
bleeding and altered bowel habits to diverticulitis. Acute diver-
ticulitis includes a spectrum of inflammation, abscess forma-
tion, bleeding, obstruction, fistula, and sepsis from perforation 
(rupture).
